output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky went up so fast that the voyagers of the Leeward boats lost their bottom. Nobody knew how deep the Upper Sea went. So a woman called Hala, whose man had gone under in the Fourteen Waters, tied a lead to a knotted line and dropped it over the stern. The line ran out through her hands. Mother Hesk, who keeps count, let out a hundred fathoms and then a hundred more, and still the lead went down. Hala's palms burned raw. Kael saw the lead falling and cast for it, and never caught it, for it is still falling. Tavo laughed at the knots and tugged them. Ennu sewed a little bell into the lead so Hala could hear it ring, and for a long time she did. Then she let go of the line, which is the only way a sounder ever learns anything. The lead is up there still, and the knots are how we count how far we have to fall back.
